data.answer:
**For standard patents, Australian residents’ share has fluctuated rather than risen steadily. It reached 9.3 per cent in 2025, up from 8.5 per cent in 2024—the highest share since 2021.**[1]

Key points over time:
- **2014–2015:** residents accounted for 8 per cent of applications in each year.[2]
- **2016 and 2019:** the resident share was around 9 per cent.[3]
- **2020–2022:** it fell to about 8 per cent in 2020, rebounded to 9 per cent in 2021, then fell to 7.7 per cent in 2022 (the complement of the reported 92.3 per cent non-resident share).[4]
- **2025:** residents filed 2,810 standard complete applications, up 9.0 per cent from 2,578 in 2024, lifting their share to 9.3 per cent.[1]

The latest report cautions that resident patenting reflects a relatively small group of R&D-intensive, technologically specialised firms, rather than being a broad barometer of Australian business activity.[5]

**Patent type matters:** residents have accounted for much larger shares of other application types—for example, 96 per cent of provisional applications and 51 per cent of innovation patent applications in 2018.[6]
